facts.fact: Dan Hixson, opened 26 April 2025: a new nine on part of the city's 1964 par-3 course.
The lake's Native name was 'waluga', meaning swan; wild swans lived there.
The developer asked for a sailboat (2026-10-22).

current.subject: A sailboat on the lake: white sails, red hull, orange pennant.
current.weaknesses: Upright and static; a block of water underneath.

concepts.name: Close-Hauled
concepts.rationale: The same boat heeled into the wind with a wake streaming astern: geometric sails, red hull, one line of lake.
concepts.symbolism: A summer afternoon on Oswego Lake, under way.
concepts.tradeoffs: Sailboats are a common lake-town motif.

concepts.name: Waluga
concepts.rationale: A wild swan with a black bill gliding on blue water: the lake's original name.
concepts.symbolism: The oldest name in town, given to its newest course.
concepts.interpretation: Trumpeter and tundra swans are the region's native swans; the drawing is generic.
concepts.typography: Fraunces Italic for a graceful, modern touch.
concepts.strengths: Elegant, specific to Lake Oswego, different from Oswego Lake CC.
concepts.tradeoffs: The link from swan to course needs the story.

recommendation: Concept 2. Waluga gives the town's public course its own identity, distinct from the private club's anchor or furnace.
